answer: On demand, by name. With d-naming, an existing session is a label record and a wanted session is its name: `zmux attach <project> <id>` covers both cases idempotently, so a manifest would only restate what the caller already types. If repeated multi-session setup ever bites, the answer is a justfile target or an elisp function calling attach N times — state that lives where the project already lives, not in zmux. Revisit only if a real project needs four sessions started in an order, which is a dependency question rather than a declaration one.
body: A manifest (project → sessions with commands and cwds) buys repeatable setup and `up`/`down`, but it is a second source of truth, which contradicts d-shape and reintroduces drift. The lazy position: no manifest.
title: Declare sessions, or create them on demand?
